lesson_title: 7 × 98 in Your Head: The Distributive Property
hook_text: 7 times 98. No calculator. Three seconds. Here's the trick that is actually a law.
clip_script: Seven friends each want a packet of 98 sweets. Nobody wants to multiply 7 by 98 directly. But 98 is 100 minus 2, so each friend gets 100 sweets minus 2 sweets. Seven friends: 7 times 100 is 700, minus 7 times 2 is 14, so 686 sweets. The 7 was shared out — distributed — to both parts of the bracket. That is the distributive property: a number outside a bracket multiplies EVERY term inside. And in a few weeks it becomes 3 times the quantity x plus 4 equals 3x plus 12 — same law, letters instead of numbers.
visual_style: A 98 splits into a bright 100 and a small red 2; a 7 slides over both and fires out 700 and 14; the 14 subtracts to leave 686, then the numbers morph into 3(x + 4) = 3x + 12.
pacing: Fast setup, deliberate split of the 98, snappy payoff, calm algebra reveal.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and learn the other two rules that let you rearrange any sum.
